skills.name: godot_character_body_3d_controller
skills.skill: Implement robust kinematic 3D player movement handling slopes, stairs, and inertia using CharacterBody3D and move_and_slide in Godot 4.7.2.
procedure: Create a CharacterBody3D node with an assigned CollisionShape3D (e.g. CapsuleShape3D).
Configure motion mode to MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED and define floor constant parameters (floor_snap_length, floor_max_angle, floor_stop_on_slope).
In _physics_process(delta), accumulate gravity using ProjectSettings.get_setting('physics/3d/default_gravity') when not on floor.
Calculate horizontal direction relative to the active Camera3D basis, project onto the horizontal plane, and normalize.
Apply acceleration and deceleration using velocity.move_toward() or Vector3.lerp() on velocity.x and velocity.z.
Invoke move_and_slide() without parameters (Godot 4 pattern). Check is_on_floor() after the slide to reset vertical velocity accumulation.
verification: Run the scene headless or via test harness: 'godot --headless --script res://tests/test_character_body_3d.gd'.
Verify velocity transitions from standstill to target velocity within the expected acceleration timeframe.
Verify character stays snapped on slopes up to floor_max_angle without falling or jittering.
pitfalls: Passing velocity into move_and_slide(velocity) — in Godot 4.x, move_and_slide takes no arguments and uses the velocity property directly.
Multiplying horizontal velocity by delta before move_and_slide() — move_and_slide implicitly applies delta to the internal velocity.
Resetting velocity.y to 0 prior to move_and_slide() on ground transitions, breaking gravity snapping.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Write a GDScript for a CharacterBody3D that implements 3D third-person movement with jump, variable slope adherence, and camera-relative direction in Godot 4.7.2.

skills.name: godot_animation_tree_state_machine
skills.skill: Construct and orchestrate node-based hierarchical animation blending and state switching using AnimationTree, AnimationMixer, and AnimationNodeStateMachine.
procedure: Attach an AnimationPlayer to provide base AnimationLibrary tracks to an AnimationTree node.
Set AnimationTree.tree_root to a new AnimationNodeStateMachine and assign anim_player to the AnimationPlayer path.
Build blend tree states (e.g. Idle, Move, Jump, Fall) and create AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition connections with appropriate switch modes and cross-fade times.
Retrieve the runtime playback object using animation_tree['parameters/playback'] as AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.
Drive state changes via playback.travel('TargetState') or set blend space coordinates using animation_tree.set('parameters/BlendSpace2D/blend_position', input_vector).
Enable the tree by setting animation_tree.active = true during _ready().
verification: Inspect playback.get_current_node() across simulated input triggers in a test script.
Assert that travel() executes smooth transitions without triggering 'Node not found' errors in console output.
Verify blend space values correctly influence playback speed and animation weighting.
pitfalls: Accessing 'parameters/playback' before the AnimationTree has been added to the SceneTree and initialized.
Using deprecated Godot 3 property path formats instead of Godot 4 unified parameters hierarchy.
Modifying AnimationPlayer directly while AnimationTree is active, leading to state desynchronization.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Create an AnimationTree state machine configuration and controller script that handles Idle, Walk/Run blend space, and Jump transitions using AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback in Godot 4.7.2.

skills.name: godot_skeleton_modifier_ik_pipeline
skills.skill: Configure procedural bone adjustments and inverse kinematics using Godot 4.7.2's SkeletonModifier3D architecture (AimModifier3D, ChainIK3D, and BoneConstraint3D).
procedure: Under the target Skeleton3D node, attach the required SkeletonModifier3D node (e.g. AimModifier3D for head tracking or ChainIK3D for limb positioning).
Set the target bone by bone name or bone index via the modifier interface.
Assign the target node path or target position Vector3 in world/local coordinate space.
Set influence weights and angular limits to prevent unnatural joint rotations.
Ensure the modifier node's 'active' property is true and execute updates in _process or _physics_process by transforming the target reference Node3D.
verification: Assert bone transforms using Skeleton3D.get_bone_global_pose() before and after modifier application.
Verify target node movement causes the end-effector bone to track the target within angle constraints without flipping.
pitfalls: Placing SkeletonModifier3D nodes outside of the Skeleton3D branch; they must be direct children of Skeleton3D.
Using legacy SkeletonIK3D which is superseded by the modular SkeletonModifier3D pipeline.
Applying bone transformations before the modifier evaluation stage without syncing Skeleton3D pose.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Set up a look-at head tracking system on a 3D character skeleton using AimModifier3D, constraining pitch and yaw angles to realistic human limits in Godot 4.7.2.

skills.name: godot_polyphonic_audio_management
skills.skill: Execute high-density, low-latency one-shot sound effects using a single AudioStreamPlayer with AudioStreamPolyphonic in Godot 4.7.2.
procedure: Create an AudioStreamPlayer node and assign its stream to an AudioStreamPolyphonic resource with defined polyphony limit (e.g. 32 voices).
Call play() on the AudioStreamPlayer in _ready() to initialize the polyphonic playback stream.
Obtain the playback controller via player.get_stream_playback() as AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic.
Trigger sound effects using playback.play_stream(stream_resource, from_offset, volume_db, pitch_scale). Store returned playback stream ID if runtime modification is required.
Adjust or terminate active voices using playback.set_stream_volume(stream_id, db) or playback.stop_stream(stream_id).
verification: Spawn 30+ simultaneous audio instances and monitor engine audio frame metrics via Performance.get_monitor(Performance.AUDIO_OUTPUT_LATENCY).
Confirm no voice dropouts occur under normal volume limits and stream IDs remain valid while playing.
pitfalls: Calling get_stream_playback() before calling player.play(); the polyphonic stream playback will be null.
Spawning dozens of individual AudioStreamPlayer nodes instead of multiplexing via AudioStreamPolyphonic, causing heavy scene-tree overhead.
Failing to cap maximum polyphony, leading to sound thread buffer starvation under intense event spam.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Implement a centralized SoundManager autoload in GDScript utilizing AudioStreamPolyphonic to play, pitch-randomize, and stop overlapping sound effects using voice IDs in Godot 4.7.2.

skills.name: godot_astar_grid_pathfinding_2d
skills.skill: Implement performant 2D grid-based pathfinding, obstacle masking, and coordinate translation using AStarGrid2D.
procedure: Instantiate an AStarGrid2D instance and define region, cell_size, and offset parameters.
Set diagonal_mode (e.g. DIAGONAL_MODE_AT_LEAST_ONE_WALKABLE or DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER) and heuristic (e.g. HEURISTIC_OCTILE).
Call update() to build the internal grid graph representation.
Mark unwalkable cells with set_point_solid(grid_coords, true) based on TileMapLayer data or static collision obstacles.
Query paths using get_point_path(start_coords, target_coords) or get_id_path(), converting between world space and grid coordinates using cell_size offsets.
verification: Create a unit test verifying path generation from origin to target avoiding a solid cell barrier.
Check that requesting a path to an unreachable target returns an empty PackedVector2Array rather than causing a hang.
pitfalls: Forgetting to call astar_grid.update() after configuring grid bounds or cell dimensions before running queries.
Passing world coordinates directly into get_point_path without dividing by cell_size or converting to Vector2i grid points.
Setting points outside the configured region, which triggers silent out-of-bounds failures or runtime assertions.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Write a GDScript utility class wrapping AStarGrid2D that synchronizes static obstacles from a TileMapLayer, supports dynamic obstacle reservation, and returns smoothed world-space paths.

skills.name: godot_compositor_custom_post_process
skills.skill: Implement custom viewport post-processing effects and compute shader passes via Godot 4.7.2's Compositor and CompositorEffect APIs.
procedure: Create a custom script extending CompositorEffect and set access_resolved_color and access_resolved_depth flags as required.
Override _render_callback(effect_callback_type, render_data) to hook into the render pipeline (e.g. EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_POST_TRANSPARENT).
Access RenderingDevice and RenderSceneBuffers to bind active render buffers and frame textures.
Dispatch compute shader pipelines or draw full-screen blits using the acquired RenderSceneBuffersRD pointers.
Instantiate a Compositor resource, append the custom CompositorEffect to compositor_effects, and assign the Compositor to WorldEnvironment.compositor or Camera3D.compositor.
verification: Attach CompositorEffect to an active Camera3D and verify visual modification in the game window.
Check engine output log for RenderingDevice validation errors or shader resource binding mismatches.
pitfalls: Executing custom rendering code without checking if render_data is valid or matches expected RenderSceneBuffersRD type.
Attempting full-screen raster passes directly inside compute callbacks without properly synchronizing texture barriers.
Failing to handle different viewport scaling modes when reading source color and depth textures.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Develop a custom CompositorEffect in GDScript for Godot 4.7.2 that applies a custom grayscale and vignette post-processing pass over the resolved scene buffer.
